_comment: Perk texts are the CURRENT rules wording, not the stale text printed on the art (Q51). Art ids map through data/assets.json.
_detailComment: quote, intro, perks[].name/when/detail and common are the setup and in-game general view (M8.1). Each line is worded after rules.md (never edited from the build) and carries its rule labels; data.js checks every label exists.

common.text: A general's bonus only applies in a battle if that general is with the army taking part in it (for an attack, with the attacking army). A general left behind in another province gives no bonus.
No general perks apply in a Senate Decree battle.

As many times as you want in a turn, during the Actions step (after the Revolt Roll), you may move your general to another of your own provinces, along the same routes as a troop Move: neutral Carthage is passable, and he pays no Gold for crossing an ally. This is free: it is not an action, and no troops need to go with him. A Move action carrying only the general is not allowed, but a troop Move can still take him along. When leaving Roma, he may move to any province you control, with or without a direct link (Roma escorts him).
Setup offers all five generals: Caesar, Scipio, Pompey, Germanicus and Augustus. A random draw uses all five. Two players cannot have the same general.

generals.name: Caesar
generals.title: Enemy Flees into the Hills
generals.text: One enemy legion flees into the hills at the start of every battle Caesar takes part in with the army (not against a lone troop). If Caesar's army wins, that troop joins him (+1 troop); if it loses or retreats the troop returns home.

perks.name: Enemy flees into the hills
perks.when: Every battle Caesar takes part in with the army, attacking or defending

detail.text: At the start of the battle the enemy force is reduced by 1 troop (legion). The troop that flees is removed from the battle: it does not fight and cannot be killed in it.

Victory bonus: when Caesar's army wins a battle, attacking or defending, Caesar gains +1 troop (the troop that ran to the hills joins him). The new troop joins the victorious troops, wherever they end up.

If Caesar's army loses or retreats, the fled troop returns home to the enemy and is not lost. If the attacker retreats from a battle against Caesar, it counts as Caesar's win, so the fled troop joins Caesar (+1).

When Caesar defends against an army that includes borrowed troops, the troop that flees is a borrowed troop if there is one. A fled borrowed troop is not dead, so it does not lower the native count and does not trigger the extra Revolt Roll: it returns home to its province's natives if Caesar loses, and joins Caesar if he wins.

Caesar cannot reduce a force to 0: if the enemy force has only 1 troop (a lone defender, or a lone attacker when Caesar defends), no troop flees, the battle is fought with dice as normal, and there is no fled-troop victory bonus.
If Caesar is not with the army in that battle, there is no effect.

generals.quote: One enemy legion will flee into the hills.

generals.name: Scipio
generals.title: Roll an Extra Die in Battle
generals.text: Attacking only, with the army: roll an extra die (4 v 2 on land, 3 v 2 by sea). It applies by itself, no choice. No perks when defending.

perks.name: Roll an extra die in battle
perks.when: Attacking only, with the army; applies by itself

detail.text: Usable on land or sea: 4 dice versus 2 on land, 3 dice versus 2 by sea.

generals.quote: One more die in every attack.

intro.text: Scipio's only perk is the extra die: there is no choice to make (the old 'add to a single die' perk was removed by Vidi, 2026-10-24).

The extra die applies ONLY when Scipio is attacking, and only if he is with the army. When Scipio is defending he gets no perks at all and has to defend the hard way: only battle Game Cards (Elephants, Moral boost) help him.

generals.name: Pompey
generals.title: Master of the Sea
generals.text: Sea attacks need no Road and roll an extra die (3 v 2), with the army. All your garrison minimums are 1 lower, always (a starting province stays at 1).

perks.name: (a) Master of the Sea
perks.when: Sea attacks, only when Pompey is with the attacking army

detail.text: Pompey's sea attacks do NOT need a Road on the province attacked from (this overrides 19.b for him).
He also gets the extra die in sea battles: when attacking by sea he rolls 3 dice versus 2 (the same as Scipio's perk 2 at sea).
Otherwise the normal sea attack rules apply.

perks.name: (b) Commands extreme loyalty
perks.when: All the time, in all of his provinces; he does not need to be present

detail.text: All of his provinces, including allied ones, have their garrison minimum lowered by 1. This stacks with the Garrison Requirement -1! card.
Exception: a starting province's minimum garrison is a flat 1, and Pompey's -1 never takes it below 1.

An allied province has no perk minimum, so for Pompey the native troops + 1 needed for its Game Roll reward drops to just its native troops, or 1 less with the Garrison Requirement -1! card, but never below 1 troop.
Exception to the native-count floor of 18.t: Pompey's garrison minimums CAN drop below the province's native troop count (also when stacked with the Garrison Requirement -1! card).
Everything based on a province's minimum garrison uses Pompey's LOWERED minimum, including which province perks are kept or lost and the revolt formula.

generals.quote: Master of the Sea, commands extreme loyalty.

generals.name: Germanicus
generals.title: Fight to the Death
generals.text: Fight to the Death: +1 to the highest die at 2 troops remaining and +2 at 1 (no cap). Defending qualifies even if the battle starts at 1 or 2. Attacking must start with at least 3 troops and be reduced to 2 or 1. Disciplined Advance (attacking only): the defender's Wall bonus is ignored for the whole battle.

perks.name: Perk 1: Fight to the Death
perks.when: Any battle, attacking or defending, with the army

detail.text: At 2 troops remaining, +1 to the highest die. At 1 troop remaining, +2 to the highest die. There is no die cap.
Defending qualifies even if the battle starts at 1 or 2 troops. Attacking must start with at least 3 and suffer losses down to 2 or 1.
If his last 2 troops are both killed in the same roll, the perk never fires.
The defender's Wall bonus is ignored for the entire battle while Germanicus attacks with the army.
Catapult Wall suppression is redundant while Disciplined Advance applies: the Wall is already ignored for the whole battle, so a Catapult is not an additional effect.

generals.quote: Fight to the Death and Disciplined Advance.

intro.text: Both perks always apply (he does not choose one, unlike Scipio), but only if Germanicus is with the army.

generals.name: Augustus
generals.title: The builder and master of the Treasury
generals.text: The builder and master of the Treasury. +1 Gold on a Merchant Bonus that was earned, and Roads cost 1 Gold.

perks.name: Perk 1: Master of the Treasury
perks.when: At the Resources step, when a Merchant Bonus is earned

detail.text: +1 Gold is added to an earned Merchant Bonus. It is never granted without a qualifying Road network.
Roads cost 1 Gold instead of 2.

generals.quote: The builder and master of the Treasury
